In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the faecal level urobilinogen may be used to monitor the effect of drugs on the intestinal microflora and to indicate the risk of super infection and failure of oral anticoceptive treatment.

the faecal concentration and/or excretion of urobilinogens should be determined in patients receiving clindamycin or dicloxacillin in combination with oral anticonception, and that a decrease in faecal excretion of uroblinogens may be an indication of a risk of superinfections or of failure of oral contraception.
a faecal level of more than 0.5 micrograms urobilinogen per gram of faeces should not be combined, in the absence of other risk factors, with oral anticonception.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of clindamycine and dicloxacilline with combined oestrogen-progestogen contraceptives may lead to a decrease in the faecal level urobilinogen.

the faecal concentration level of urobilogen may be a useful tool in the investigation of the influence of antibiotics on the bowel microflora and on the oestrogen-metabolism in the bowel, and thus may be a valuable indicator for the risk of a superinfection and failure of the oral anticonception.
